recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. # v0.1 reconstruction: library brief (HandlePool v0.5, DataStack DS-v2)

Read first: `SP/v01/kernel-brief.md` (context, hard rules, kernel design), `SP/v01/arena-ref-brief.md`
(arena changes, notably `NewArenaBase` now carrying v0.1 §76.6), `SP/v01/arbitration.md` (Q3, Q4, Q5,
Q11, Q12, Q21 W1, Q23, Q27, Q28 and the two follow-up answers), and the reports in
`SP/v01/kernel-report.md` and `SP/v01/arena-report.md`.
`SP=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/ref`.

Both contracts are local, non-normative library contracts. Docstrings cite the applicable spec
clauses (v0.1) and the contract identifier: "HandlePool v0.5" or "DS-v2", stated as non-normative.
Agents H (`formal/Ern/Lib/HandlePool.lean`) and D (`formal/Ern/Lib/DataStack.lean`) run in parallel:
never run `lake build`; check with `cd formal && ~/.elan/bin/lake env lean Ern/Lib/<File>.lean`.
Do not touch corpus files (the corpus phase follows).

## HandlePool v0.5 = HandlePool v0.4 annex (Annex D of `~/Downloads/ERN_MM-03.3_v0.4_pour_validation.md`, lines 687–725) with these changes

- HP5-1 `freeSlot` (Q3). Preconditions: administration right (`AdminRight`: live pool, `MetaRight` =
  `Modify` exercisable on the pool value, §36); valid handle; no leaf of the entry is `Init` (each is
  `Uninit` or `Moved`); no active authority derived from a companion of this pool (a strict
  descendant of a companion recorded for this pool) covers a leaf of the entry. Effect: the slot
  becomes free and its generation is incremented; NO end-of-use effect: the kernel state is unchanged.
  Outcome order: keep the existing order of `FreeSlotStep` (`reject` without pool or right, then `fail`
  on an invalid handle, then `reject` on the content conditions); Q5 concerns resolution (§89) and is
  not extended to `freeSlot` (report this as a point for the user).
  Remove what only served the v0.4 `freeSlot`: `Exempt`, `DyingAccessOK`, `ContentAnchorOK`,
  `ContentEndPre`, `contentEnd_*`, `freeSlot_preserves*` on `endUseEff`, `freeSlot_lands_in_reachable`
  and the HP-4 step-level discussion (moot: no kernel effect), and the v0.4 obligation
  `pool_freeSlot_ends_content`.
- HP5-2 Mandatory proof (1) (Q3, follow-up): a complete witness from `PState.init statics` by accepted
  steps: `newPool`, `allocSlot`, `resolve` in `Modify`, a write of the entry through the resolved entry
  authority (kernel `write`), `transfer` of the entry's value to a local of the same shape, `unresolve`,
  then `freeSlot` accepted. `internal` must be DERIVED (as in the corpus pools: derived from the
  storage root and stored in the pool value). The transfer relies on the v0.1 §63.4 exemption (the
  entry, the companion, `internal` and its origins ground the right). "Local": prefer a place created
  by `enterFrame` (§72) owned by the current frame; if that is infeasible in the run, use a static
  `Uninit` place directly owned by frame 0 and say why in the docstring and report.
- HP5-3 Mandatory proof (2) (Q3): the metadata update of `freeSlot` (free state, generation) is
  realizable by an authorized write under the administration right: for every library-reachable state
  and pool with `AdminRight`, the kernel `write` (§67, `Write3Pre`) of the leaves of the pool value
  (the place holding `internal`) is accepted. If the effect of that write is the identity on the
  kernel state (the pool value's leaves are `Init`, §76.5), state it too.
- HP5-4 Per-pool guarantees (Q4): D.2 ("une compagne `Modify` active bloque les nouvelles compagnes"),
  the `freeSlot` content condition, and D.4(3) ("`freeSlot` n'aboutit jamais si une descendante active
  d'une compagne couvre le slot") concern the companions of the slot's pool. `PoolInv` = entries
  disjoint and in the storage + `pool_no_stale_access` + the per-pool `freeSlot` guarantee;
  `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive` per pool. Nested pools stay allowed. Remove the v0.4 literal versions
  and their refutation witnesses (n10, e*/g* entry routes, `*_false`), keeping the `*_same_pool`
  results under their new names.
- HP5-5 Resolution order (Q5): handle validation precedes the right check: `resolve` and `resolveMany`
  give `fail` on an invalid handle before checking `ResolveRight`. A handle of a dead pool (internal
  inactive) is stale: `fail`. A missing pool index stays `reject`.
- HP5-6 (Q12): a handle of a free entry is stale: `fail` (the slot is not live; after the new
  `freeSlot` its generation also differs).
- HP5-7 Kernel guarantees on the whole state (Q4, O5.g): `KernelGuarantee` (every kernel state of a
  library run satisfies `KInv`) proved without `PReachI`: every library step's kernel effect is a
  sequence of accepted kernel steps (or the identity). Remove `PReachI` if nothing needs it.
- Keep and re-prove: composite borrow (O5.a), `resolveMany` Observe/distinctness (O5.b), `newPool`
  needs `Uninit` storage and `NewArenaBase` (O5.c), stale/other-pool/atomicity/distinctness (O5.h),
  `pool_no_stale_access`, `pool_entries_disjoint`, §56 results.

## DataStack DS-v2 = DS-v1 with these changes

DS-v1 (brief): "Marks carry stack identity and a fresh mark identifier; the stack keeps the ordered list
of live marks; rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark, rejects if an active authority derived from
internal covers a cell above m, otherwise returns those cells to available and removes m and every
mark above it; push and grow use the derived issue; grow is in place only (same base, extension into
the space directly after the block, fail otherwise)." Readings: `SP/readings/datastack.md` DS-R1–DS-R13.

- DS2-1 (Q11 d, DS-R10): `mark` requires `AdminRight` on the stack (else `reject`); missing stack
  `reject`.
- DS2-2 (Q11 e, DS-R11): `grow` stores the new block authority into the place that currently holds the
  block authority `b` (not the recorded `Blk.dst`). Update the metadata accordingly.
- DS2-3 (Q28 c, DS-R13): a dead stack (internal inactive) invalidates its marks: `rewind` of a mark of

## Context

- Repository `/Users/guygouri/Devlab/ernlang/ern`, branch `reference/memory-model-v0`. Lake project `formal/`
  (Lean 4, no Mathlib). Build from `formal/` with `~/.elan/bin/lake`.

  `SP=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/ref`.
  Read the clauses you touch in the v0.1 file and the arbitration file before editing.
- Previous obligation map (v0 era, for orientation only): `SP/table-final.md`.

## Hard rules (in addition to AGENTS.md)

- No `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom`, `native_decide`, `noncomputable`, `set_option`. No warnings.
- Every constant's axioms must be within {propext, Quot.sound}. `Classical.choice` is NOT allowed. Avoid
  `Classical`, `by_contra` on non-decidable props, `Decidable.byContradiction` on classical instances,
  `simp` lemmas that pull `Classical.choice` (check if unsure with `#print axioms` in a scratch file
  under `SP/`).
- Every def/theorem docstring cites the clause it formalizes (`§63.9`, `§69.2`, ...). Module headers that
  name the spec file must name `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md`.
- Everything in English. Do not commit; do not touch git state (no stash, checkout, reset).
- Never weaken a statement, never add an unjustified hypothesis, never change a definition to make a
  proof go through. If a proof is stuck on a goal you believe false, build a concrete counterexample
  (a `decide`-checked state) if you can, stop and report the goal state.
- New helper lemmas you add to a file that other agents do not own must be `private` or carry a
  file-specific prefix, so that two files never define the same public name.

## Fixed design (decided by the orchestrator; do not deviate, report instead)

D1 Pinning obligations (v0.1 §74, §75; arbitration Q23 B#45).
  - In `Basic.lean`, add
    `structure PinOb where place : Nat; leaves : List Nat; active : Bool` (deriving DecidableEq, Repr):
    a dynamic pinning obligation, its identity being its index in `S3.pins`.
  - Replace the field `S3.pin : Nat → Bool` by `pins : List PinOb`.
  - Define `S3.pin (s : S3) (l : Nat) : Bool := s.pins.any fun o => o.active && o.leaves.contains l`
    (a leaf is dynamically pinned while an active obligation covers it), so that existing uses
    `s.pin l = false` keep their meaning.
  - `pinEff s p := { s with pins := s.pins ++ [⟨p, footprint s.P p, true⟩] }` (fresh identity = index).
  - `unpin` takes an obligation identity `o`. Effect: obligation `o` becomes inactive, nothing else changes.
    `UnpinPre k s o`: obligation `o` exists and is active; its place is usable; `HasRight s .modify place`;
    `k.ExternalDone o`.
  - `K.ExternalDone : Nat → Prop` keeps its type; it now applies to obligation identities (fix docstring).
  - `enterEff`, `allocEff`, `S3.init` no longer touch pins (`S3.init`: `pins := []`).
  - `PinPre` unchanged.
D2 Grounding of a right (v0.1 §63.4, §69.2, §70.3; follow-up answer "Q3 (suite)").
  - `Grounds (s : S3) (m : Mode) (q g : Nat) : Prop :=`
    `g ∈ List.range s.A.length ∧ s.ExercisableAt g m ∧ ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, Allows (effective s g l) m`
    (HasRight s m q ↔ ∃ g, Grounds s m q g; prove this lemma).
  - `RightChain (s : S3) (g j : Nat) : Prop := j = g ∨ j ∈ s.ancs g` (`ancs` = strict ancestors).
  - Both decidable. Place them in `Basic.lean` (after `HasRight`) or `Ops.lean`.
D3 `TransferPre` (Ops.lean).
  - Keep `srcRight : HasRight s .modify src`.
  - `noOutsideDerived` becomes: `∃ g ∈ List.range s.A.length, Grounds s .modify src g ∧`
    `∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, ActiveDerivedOutside s src j → RightChain s g j` (v0.1 §63.4).
  - New field `dstUsableAfter : (transferEff s src dst).Usable dst` (v0.1 §63.9).
D4 `EndUsePre` (Ops.lean).
  - `access` becomes: `∃ g ∈ List.range s.A.length, Grounds s .modify p g ∧`
    `∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, RightChain s g j ∨ EndUseAccessOK s p j` (v0.1 §69.2, exemption).
  - New field `keptDesc : ∀ a ∈ List.range s.A.length, ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, s.Active a →`
    `¬ (endUseEff s p).Active a → a ∈ s.ancs j → ¬ (endUseEff s p).Active j` (v0.1 §69.2, last
    sentence: an authority the step makes inactive keeps no active descendant).
D5 `FreePre` (Ops.lean): same two changes, with `FreeAccessOK` and `freeEff` (v0.1 §70.3).
D6 `AllocStatic` (Ops.lean): new field `providerUsable : s.Usable provider` (v0.1 §71.2).
D7 `DerivePre` (Ops.lean): new field `chainActive : ∀ x ∈ s.ancs src, s.Active x` (v0.1 §60.1: every
   authority of the origin chain, effective anchor included, is active; `src` itself is `active`).
D8 `I2` (Invariants.lean, v0.1 §51): add the conjunct `(y.active = true → x.active = true)` for the origin
   `x` of `y`. Keep the mode and footprint conjuncts.
D9 `I5` (Invariants.lean, v0.1 §57), quantified over the leaves of the state ("every pinned leaf"):
   `def I5 (k : K) (s : S3) : Prop := ∀ l, l < s.P.length → isLeaf s.P l → (k.Pinned l ∨ s.pin l = true) →`
   `∃ q, s.Usable q ∧ l ∈ footprint s.P q`.
   (Revised after the kernel review: the first version quantified over every index, so it also
   constrained `K.Pinned` on indices that are not leaves of the state, which §57 does not say.)
   It is not part of `KInv` (§57 keeps I5 a specialized obligation of `K.Pinned`). Its reachability
   theorem carries no hypothesis on `K.Pinned` beyond what the proof needs (report any).
D10 `StaticsOK` (Invariants.lean): docstring now cites v0.1 §47 (acyclic ownership of statics) and §49
   (ordering of identifiers used to represent well-foundedness). Definition unchanged.
D11 Auxiliary invariants: `KAux`, `HeldAnchored` and any new auxiliary invariant you need (for example
   "every obligation's leaves are existing leaves") are allowed only as auxiliary, documented as "not a
   clause of §57", and must be proved to hold initially and to be preserved by every step, so that the
   §57 statement on reachable states carries no extra hypothesis.
D12 Theorems expected at the end of the kernel phase (Main.lean):
   - every step preserves `KInv` from states satisfying `KInv` and the auxiliaries (DDSound for split);
     `transfer` is no longer an exception;
   - `reachable_kinv : DDSound k → StaticsOK statics → Reachable k statics s → KInv s` (no other hypothesis);
   - I5 on reachable states (D9);
   - the v0 counterexample run of §63 (ownership cycle through `transfer`, previously
     `transfer_breaks_kinv`/`reachable_kinv_false`) is rejected under v0.1 by §63.9: keep it as a
     witness theorem stating the rejection;
   - remove what v0.1 makes obsolete: `reachable_kinv_false`, `KStepDU`, `ReachableDU` and their
     theorems, `transfer_kinv_iff` (replace by plain preservation);
   - keep: step/reachable correspondence, `op_fail_only_alloc`, base frame, `init_kinv`, `init_statics`,
     `init_only_by_writes`, `init_history`, `exitFrame_no_dangling`, `call_params_effective_protected`,
     `effective_exclusive`, and every other v0 obligation theorem, re-proved.

## File ownership and build protocol

- Stage 1 (one agent): `Basic.lean`, `Ops.lean`, `Invariants.lean`, `Lemmas.lean`, `Preserve/Common.lean`

Q9 (suite) : règle unifiée. endUse et free sont rejetés si une autorité qu'ils désactivent — détenue par un emplacement qui meurt, stockage possédé transitivement compris, ou racine d'un stockage libéré — a un descendant actif, quelle que soit son empreinte, que le même pas ne désactive pas. Les cas (1) et (2) sont donc rejetés. La sortie de cadre garde son ré-ancrage, et rejette si aucune origine survivante n'existe (inchangé). I2 au sens « origine active » tient après chaque pas.

Q3 (suite) : remplace Q17. - DS-R4 : grow avec extra = 0 est ok (réémission en place de la même région) ;
- DS-R3 : rewind sur un indice de pile inexistant donne fail, comme une marque invalide (cohérent avec Q5 et Q28).

4	/-!
5	# DataStack: a library administrative abstraction (contract DS-v2, non-normative)
6	
7	A `DataStack` instance of `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md`. The spec does not define
8	its contract (Part XIV preamble: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their
9	library abstractions and are not defined here"). The contract formalized here is the library
10	contract **DS-v2**, which is **not normative**: every definition below that encodes a DS-v2 item
11	says so. The normative clauses that constrain it are §36 (`MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable
12	on the stack value; the abstraction adds no rights to the kernel), §38 and §46 (library state
13	separate from `S₃`), §47 (empty initial registry), §56 (guard over all registries of live
14	administrations) and §58 (outcomes).
15	
16	DS-v2 is DS-v1 with six changes. DS-v1: marks carry the stack identity and a fresh mark
17	identifier; the stack keeps the ordered list of live marks; `rewind m` fails on a dead or foreign
18	mark, rejects if an active authority derived from `internal` covers a cell above `m`, otherwise
19	returns those cells to available and removes `m` and every mark above it; `push` and `grow` use the
20	derived `issue` of Part XIV (`Arena.IssueD`: its static checks, the availability `fail`, then
21	`split` of `internal` and `store` of the block); `grow` is in place only (same base, extension into
22	the space directly after the block, `fail` otherwise). DS2-1: `mark` requires the administrative
23	right of §36 (`AdminRight`), else `reject`. DS2-2: `grow` stores the new block authority into the
24	place that currently holds the block authority `b`. DS2-3: a dead stack (`internal` inactive)
25	invalidates its marks, so `rewind` of a mark of a dead stack is `fail`, checked with the dead or
26	foreign mark, before the right. DS2-4: "a cell above m" is every cell at a position `≥ m.top`.
27	DS2-5: `grow` with `extra = 0` is accepted, an in-place reissue of the same region. DS2-6: `rewind`
28	on a stack index that does not exist is `fail`, like an invalid mark (`mark`, `push` and `grow` on
29	a missing stack stay `reject`). Also part of DS-v2: `push` without room is `fail`; `grow` of a `b`
30	that is no block of the stack is `reject`; §76.5 applies to `newStack`; the dead or foreign mark is
31	checked before the right of §36; §36 applies to `rewind`.
32	
33	Every `ok` step of the library is a sequence of kernel steps O1–O16 (`DReach.reachable`), so the
34	abstraction adds no rights to the kernel (§36).
35	-/
36	
37	namespace Ern.Lib.DataStack
38	
39	open Ern.MemoryModel Ern.MemoryModel.Access Ern.MemoryModel.Arena
40	
41	/-! ## Library state (DS-v2; §38, §46, §47) -/
42	
43	/-- A block issued by a stack (DS-v2, non-normative; recorded like the issuances of §46): position
44	`base` of its first cell and number `size` of cells among the ordered cells of the stack, block
45	authority `auth`, destination `dst` that received it (at `push`, or at the `grow` that issued it,
46	DS2-2). -/
47	structure Blk where
48	  base : Nat
49	  size : Nat
50	  auth : Nat
51	  dst : Nat
52	deriving DecidableEq, Repr
53	
54	/-- A mark (DS-v2, non-normative: "marks carry stack identity and a fresh mark identifier";
55	library metadata of an administrative abstraction, §36, §38): the identity of its stack, its fresh
56	identifier, the top of the stack when it was taken. -/
57	structure Mark where
58	  stack : Nat
59	  id : Nat
60	  top : Nat
61	deriving DecidableEq, Repr
62	
63	/-- A stack (DS-v2, non-normative; library state, §38, §46): administered storage, `internal`
64	authority held by the stack value (§36), ordered cells (the leaves of the storage at creation),
65	top (the cells at positions `≥ top` are available), issued blocks (oldest first), and the ordered
66	list of live marks (DS-v2: "the stack keeps the ordered list of live marks"). -/
67	structure Stack where
68	  storage : Nat
69	  internal : Nat
70	  cells : List Nat
71	  top : Nat
72	  blocks : List Blk
73	  marks : List Mark
74	deriving DecidableEq, Repr
75	
76	/-- State of the stack library (DS-v2, non-normative; §38: administrative states of library
77	abstractions are separate from `S₃`): the kernel state, the stack registry (a stack is identified
78	by its index; stacks are never removed) and the next fresh mark identifier. -/
79	structure DState where
80	  kern : S3
81	  stacks : List Stack
82	  fresh : Nat
83	
84	/-- Initial state (§47: the kernel's initial state; the library registry starts empty; DS-v2,
85	non-normative: no mark identifier given out). -/
86	def DState.init (statics : Statics) : DState := ⟨S3.init statics, [], 0⟩
87	
88	/-- The `n` cells from position `b` of the stack, leaves of the administered storage (§46; DS-v2,
89	non-normative). -/
90	def cellsOf (st : Stack) (b n : Nat) : List Nat := (st.cells.drop b).take n
91	
92	/-- The cells above mark `m` (DS-v2, non-normative, "a cell above m", DS2-4: every cell at a
93	position `≥ m.top`; §46 available leaves): `rewind m` returns those below the current top to
94	available, the others already are. -/
95	def above (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : List Nat := st.cells.drop m.top
96	
97	/-- The stack seen as an administration entry (§46, §36; DS-v2, non-normative): storage,
98	`internal`, available cells (positions `≥ top`) and issued blocks. Used for `MetaRight` and the
99	static checks of the derived `issue`, which read only the storage and `internal`. -/
100	def Stack.entry (st : Stack) : ArenaEntry :=
101	  ⟨st.storage, st.internal, st.cells.drop st.top,
102	    st.blocks.map fun x => (cellsOf st x.base x.size, x.auth)⟩
103	
104	/-- The block of the stack whose authority is `b` (§46 issuances; DS-v2, non-normative). -/
105	def Stack.block (st : Stack) (b : Nat) : Option Blk := st.blocks.find? fun y => decide (y.auth = b)
106	
107	/-- A live mark of stack `j` (DS-v2, non-normative: a mark that is neither dead nor foreign; it
108	decides the `fail` case of `rewind`, §58): the stack is live (`internal` is active, §46 read for a
109	stack; DS2-3: a dead stack invalidates its marks), the mark names stack `j` and it belongs to the
110	list of live marks of the stack. -/
111	def LiveMark (s : S3) (j : Nat) (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : Prop :=
112	  s.Active st.internal ∧ m.stack = j ∧ m ∈ st.marks
113	
114	/-- Decidability of `LiveMark` (§58; DS-v2). -/
115	instance (s : S3) (j : Nat) (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : Decidable (LiveMark s j st m) := by
116	  unfold LiveMark; infer_instance
117	
118	/-- The administrative right of §36 for a stack (DS-v2, non-normative, with §36 and §46 read for a
119	stack): the stack is live (`internal` is active) and `MetaRight`, `Modify` exercisable on the stack
120	value, the place holding `internal`. -/
121	def AdminRight (s : S3) (st : Stack) : Prop := s.Active st.internal ∧ MetaRight s st.entry
122	
123	/-- Decidability of `AdminRight` (§36; DS-v2). -/
124	instance (s : S3) (st : Stack) : Decidable (AdminRight s st) := by
125	  unfold AdminRight; infer_instance
126	
127	/-! ## `newStack` and the guard of §56 -/
128	
129	/-- The stack registry as a registry of live administrations (§56; DS-v2, non-normative): the
130	`internal` identities of its live stacks. -/
131	def stackInternals (s : S3) (stacks : List Stack) : List Nat :=
132	  (stacks.filter fun st => decide (s.Active st.internal)).map (·.internal)
133	
134	/-- Preconditions of `newStack(storage, internal)` (DS-v2, non-normative; §56): those of `newArena`
135	other than its guard (`NewArenaBase`, §76.1–§76.3, §76.5 and §76.6 read for a stack), and the guard
136	of §56 over the stack registry and every other registry of live administrations `others`. -/
137	structure NewStackPre (s : S3) (stacks : List Stack) (others : List (List Nat))
138	    (storage internal : Nat) : Prop where
139	  /-- §76.1–§76.3, §76.5, §76.6, read for a stack (DS-v2). -/
140	  base : NewArenaBase s storage internal
141	  /-- §56: no live administration of any registry uses `internal`. -/
142	  guard : Guard56 (stackInternals s stacks :: others) internal
143	
144	/-- Decidability of `NewStackPre` (§56; DS-v2). -/
145	instance (s : S3) (stacks : List Stack) (others : List (List Nat)) (storage internal : Nat) :
146	    Decidable (NewStackPre s stacks others storage internal) :=
147	  decidable_of_iff (NewArenaBase s storage internal ∧
148	    Guard56 (stackInternals s stacks :: others) internal)
149	    ⟨fun ⟨a, b⟩ => ⟨a, b⟩, fun ⟨a, b⟩ => ⟨a, b⟩⟩
150	
151	/-- Effect of `newStack` (DS-v2, non-normative; §36: registration adds no rights): a stack whose
152	cells are the leaves of the storage, top 0, no block, no mark; the kernel state is unchanged. -/
153	def newStackEff (D : DState) (storage internal : Nat) : DState :=
154	  { D with stacks := D.stacks ++ [⟨storage, internal, footprint D.kern.P storage, 0, [], []⟩] }
155	
156	/-- `newStack` as a relation (DS-v2, non-normative; §56, §58): `ok` or `reject`. -/
157	def NewStackStep (others : List (List Nat)) (storage internal : Nat) (D : DState) :
158	    Outcome3 DState → Prop :=
159	  Guarded (NewStackPre D.kern D.stacks others storage internal) (newStackEff D storage internal)
160	
161	/-! ## `push` (DS-v2: the derived `issue`, Part XIV, §77) -/
162	
163	/-- Metadata after `push` (DS-v2, non-normative; as the `ok` effect of §77 on §46 metadata): the
164	cells leave the available part (the top rises by `size`), the block is recorded. -/
165	def pushMeta (st : Stack) (size a dst : Nat) : Stack :=
166	  { st with top := st.top + size, blocks := st.blocks ++ [⟨st.top, size, a, dst⟩] }
167	
168	/-- `push(j, size, dst)` (DS-v2, non-normative: "push uses the derived issue"): the derived `issue`
169	of Part XIV (`Arena.IssueD`) of the `size` cells at the top into `dst`, on the stack seen as an
170	entry: its static checks (`IssueStatic`, §77.1, §77.2, with `MetaRight` of §36), then `fail`, the
171	state unchanged, when fewer than `size` cells are left (availability, §77.4; DS-v2, Q11 (a)),
172	then `split` of `internal` on the cells (O2) and `store` of the block, of fresh identity `|A|`, into
173	`dst` (O8). -/
174	inductive PushStep (k : K) (j size dst : Nat) (D : DState) : Outcome3 DState → Prop where
175	  | noStack : D.stacks[j]? = none → PushStep k j size dst D .reject
176	  | static {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
177	      ¬ IssueStatic D.kern st.entry (cellsOf st st.top size) dst → PushStep k j size dst D .reject
178	  | fail {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
179	      IssueStatic D.kern st.entry (cellsOf st st.top size) dst →
180	      ¬ st.top + size ≤ st.cells.length → PushStep k j size dst D .fail
181	  | split {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
182	      IssueStatic D.kern st.entry (cellsOf st st.top size) dst →
183	      st.top + size ≤ st.cells.length →
184	      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st st.top size] D.kern .reject →
185	      PushStep k j size dst D .reject
186	  | store {st : Stack} {s₁ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
187	      IssueStatic D.kern st.entry (cellsOf st st.top size) dst →
188	      st.top + size ≤ st.cells.length →
189	      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st st.top size] D.kern (.ok s₁) →
190	      StoreStep D.kern.A.length dst s₁ .reject → PushStep k j size dst D .reject
191	  | ok {st : Stack} {s₁ s₂ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
192	      IssueStatic D.kern st.entry (cellsOf st st.top size) dst →
193	      st.top + size ≤ st.cells.length →
194	      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st st.top size] D.kern (.ok s₁) →
195	      StoreStep D.kern.A.length dst s₁ (.ok s₂) →
196	      PushStep k j size dst D
197	        (.ok ⟨s₂, D.stacks.set j (pushMeta st size D.kern.A.length dst), D.fresh⟩)
198	
199	/-! ## `mark` (DS-v2) -/
200	
201	/-- Metadata after `mark` (DS-v2, non-normative; library metadata, §36, §38): a mark naming stack
202	`j`, with the fresh identifier `fresh` and the current top, is appended to the live marks. -/
203	def markMeta (j : Nat) (st : Stack) (fresh : Nat) : Stack :=
204	  { st with marks := st.marks ++ [⟨j, fresh, st.top⟩] }
205	
206	/-- `mark(j)` (DS-v2, non-normative; §58 outcomes): `reject` on a missing stack; `reject` without
207	the administrative right of §36 (DS2-1); otherwise `ok`, metadata only (no right created, §36), the
208	identifier is fresh. -/
209	inductive MarkStep (j : Nat) (D : DState) : Outcome3 DState → Prop where
210	  | noStack : D.stacks[j]? = none → MarkStep j D .reject
211	  | static {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → ¬ AdminRight D.kern st → MarkStep j D .reject
212	  | ok {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → AdminRight D.kern st →
213	      MarkStep j D (.ok ⟨D.kern, D.stacks.set j (markMeta j st D.fresh), D.fresh + 1⟩)
214	
215	/-- `mark_rejects_without_right` (DS-v2, non-normative, DS2-1: `mark` requires `AdminRight` on the
216	stack, else `reject`; §36, §58): on an existing stack without the administrative right of §36,
217	`mark` has the outcome `reject` and no other. -/
218	theorem mark_rejects_without_right {j : Nat} {D : DState} {st : Stack}
219	    (hst : D.stacks[j]? = some st) (ha : ¬ AdminRight D.kern st) :
220	    MarkStep j D .reject ∧ ∀ o, MarkStep j D o → o = .reject := by
221	  refine ⟨.static hst ha, fun o ho => ?_⟩
222	  cases ho with
223	  | noStack => rfl
224	  | static => rfl
225	  | ok h ha' => rw [hst] at h; cases h; exact absurd ha' ha
226	
227	/-! ## `rewind` (DS-v2) -/
228	
229	/-- Metadata after `rewind m` (DS-v2, non-normative; as the `ok` effect of §78 on §46 metadata):
230	the cells above `m` return to available (the top returns to the top of `m`), the blocks from that
231	top are forgotten, `m` and every later mark are removed. -/
232	def rewindMeta (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : Stack :=
233	  { st with
234	    top := m.top
235	    blocks := st.blocks.filter fun x => decide (x.base < m.top)
236	    marks := st.marks.takeWhile fun x => decide (x ≠ m) }
237	
238	/-- `rewind(j, m)` (DS-v2, non-normative): `fail`, the state unchanged, on a missing stack (DS2-6)
239	and on a dead or foreign mark, a mark of a dead stack included (DS2-3), before the right; `reject`
240	without the administrative right of §36; then the derived `reset` of Part XIV on the cells above
241	`m` (DS2-4): `split` of `internal` on them (O2), which rejects when an active authority derived from
242	`internal` covers one of them (`rewind_rejects_live_above`), and `release` of the derived authority
243	(O3); `ok`: the cells return to available, `m` and the later marks are removed. -/
244	inductive RewindStep (k : K) (j : Nat) (m : Mark) (D : DState) : Outcome3 DState → Prop where
245	  | noStack : D.stacks[j]? = none → RewindStep k j m D .fail
246	  | dead {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → ¬ LiveMark D.kern j st m →
247	      RewindStep k j m D .fail
248	  | static {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → LiveMark D.kern j st m →
249	      ¬ AdminRight D.kern st → RewindStep k j m D .reject
250	  | split {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → LiveMark D.kern j st m → AdminRight D.kern st →
251	      SplitStep k st.internal [above st m] D.kern .reject → RewindStep k j m D .reject
252	  | release {st : Stack} {s₁ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → LiveMark D.kern j st m →
253	      AdminRight D.kern st → SplitStep k st.internal [above st m] D.kern (.ok s₁) →
254	      ReleaseStep D.kern.A.length s₁ .reject → RewindStep k j m D .reject
255	  | ok {st : Stack} {s₁ s₂ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → LiveMark D.kern j st m →
256	      AdminRight D.kern st → SplitStep k st.internal [above st m] D.kern (.ok s₁) →
257	      ReleaseStep D.kern.A.length s₁ (.ok s₂) →
258	      RewindStep k j m D (.ok ⟨s₂, D.stacks.set j (rewindMeta st m), D.fresh⟩)
259	
260	/-- `rewind` has one outcome (§58: a guarded transition has one outcome; DS-v2, non-normative):
261	the cases of `RewindStep` exclude each other, the two `fail` cases (missing stack, DS2-6; dead or
262	foreign mark) give the same outcome, and `split` and `release` are deterministic (`Guarded.det`).
263	With `rewind_ok_iff`, an `ok` rewind is never also `reject` or `fail`. -/
264	theorem RewindStep.det {k : K} {j : Nat} {m : Mark} {D : DState} {o₁ o₂ : Outcome3 DState}
265	    (h₁ : RewindStep k j m D o₁) (h₂ : RewindStep k j m D o₂) : o₁ = o₂ := by
266	  cases h₁ with
267	  | noStack h =>
268	    cases h₂ with
269	    | noStack _ => rfl
270	    | dead _ _ => rfl
271	    | static h' _ _ => rw [h] at h'; cases h'
272	    | split h' _ _ _ => rw [h] at h'; cases h'
273	    | release h' _ _ _ _ => rw [h] at h'; cases h'
274	    | ok h' _ _ _ _ => rw [h] at h'; cases h'
275	  | dead h hl =>
276	    cases h₂ with
277	    | noStack _ => rfl
278	    | dead _ _ => rfl
279	    | static h' hl' _ => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd hl' hl
280	    | split h' hl' _ _ => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd hl' hl
281	    | release h' hl' _ _ _ => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd hl' hl
282	    | ok h' hl' _ _ _ => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd hl' hl
283	  | static h hl ha =>
284	    cases h₂ with
285	    | noStack h' => rw [h] at h'; cases h'
286	    | dead h' hl' => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd hl hl'
287	    | static _ _ _ => rfl
288	    | split _ _ _ _ => rfl
289	    | release _ _ _ _ _ => rfl
290	    | ok h' _ ha' _ _ => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd ha' ha
291	  | split h hl _ hs =>
292	    cases h₂ with
293	    | noStack h' => rw [h] at h'; cases h'
294	    | dead h' hl' => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd hl hl'
295	    | static _ _ _ => rfl
296	    | split _ _ _ _ => rfl
297	    | release _ _ _ _ _ => rfl
298	    | ok h' _ _ hs' _ => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; cases Guarded.det hs hs'
299	  | release h hl _ hs hr =>
300	    cases h₂ with
301	    | noStack h' => rw [h] at h'; cases h'
302	    | dead h' hl' => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd hl hl'
303	    | static _ _ _ => rfl
304	    | split _ _ _ _ => rfl
305	    | release _ _ _ _ _ => rfl
306	    | ok h' _ _ hs' hr' =>
307	      rw [h] at h'; cases h'; cases Guarded.det hs hs'; cases Guarded.det hr hr'
308	  | ok h hl ha hs hr =>
309	    cases h₂ with
310	    | noStack h' => rw [h] at h'; cases h'
311	    | dead h' hl' => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd hl hl'
312	    | static h' _ ha' => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd ha ha'
313	    | split h' _ _ hs' => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; cases Guarded.det hs hs'
314	    | release h' _ _ hs' hr' =>
315	      rw [h] at h'; cases h'; cases Guarded.det hs hs'; cases Guarded.det hr hr'
316	    | ok h' _ _ hs' hr' =>
317	      rw [h] at h'; cases h'; cases Guarded.det hs hs'; cases Guarded.det hr hr'; rfl
318	
319	/-- `rewind_missing_fails` (DS-v2, non-normative, DS2-6: `rewind` on a stack index that does not
320	exist is `fail`, like an invalid mark, before the right of §36; §58 `fail`): on a missing stack,
321	`rewind m` fails, with no other outcome, for every mark `m`. -/
322	theorem rewind_missing_fails {k : K} {D : DState} {j : Nat} {m : Mark}
323	    (h : D.stacks[j]? = none) :
324	    RewindStep k j m D .fail ∧ ∀ o, RewindStep k j m D o → o = .fail :=
325	  ⟨.noStack h, fun _ ho => ho.det (.noStack h)⟩
326	
327	/-! ## `grow` (DS-v2: in place, the derived `issue`) -/
328	
329	/-- In-place extension (DS-v2, non-normative: "extension into the space directly after the
330	block"; the availability check of the derived `issue`, §77.4): `extra` is zero, the empty
331	extension, always available (§77.4: "The empty region is always available"; DS2-5: an in-place
332	reissue of the same region), or the block ends at the top and `extra` available cells follow it. -/
333	def InPlace (st : Stack) (x : Blk) (extra : Nat) : Prop :=
334	  extra = 0 ∨ (x.base + x.size = st.top ∧ st.top + extra ≤ st.cells.length)
335	
336	/-- Decidability of `InPlace` (§77.4; DS-v2). -/
337	instance (st : Stack) (x : Blk) (extra : Nat) : Decidable (InPlace st x extra) := by
338	  unfold InPlace; infer_instance
339	
340	/-- The grown block (DS-v2, non-normative: same base, `extra` more cells, new authority `a`,
341	destination `d`, the place that held the authority of the block, DS2-2; an issuance of §46). -/
342	def growBlk (x : Blk) (extra a d : Nat) : Blk := ⟨x.base, x.size + extra, a, d⟩
343	
344	/-- Metadata after `grow` (DS-v2, non-normative; as the `ok` effect of §77 on §46 metadata): the
345	top rises by `extra`; the block is replaced by the grown block. -/
346	def growMeta (st : Stack) (x : Blk) (extra a d : Nat) : Stack :=
347	  { st with
348	    top := st.top + extra
349	    blocks := st.blocks.map fun y => if y.auth = x.auth then growBlk x extra a d else y }
350	
351	/-- The place that holds authority `a`, if a place holds it (§42: holder; DS-v2, non-normative,
352	DS2-2: the destination of `grow` is the place that currently holds the block authority). -/
353	def holderPlace (s : S3) (a : Nat) : Option Nat :=
354	  match s.A[a]? with
355	  | some y => match y.holder with
356	    | .place v => some v
357	    | .frame _ => none
358	  | none => none
359	
360	/-- `grow(j, b, extra)` (DS-v2, non-normative: in place only, using the derived `issue`): `reject`
361	when `b` is not a block of the stack; `extra` may be zero, an in-place reissue of the same region
362	(DS2-5); `release` of `b` (O3); then the derived
363	`issue` of Part XIV (`Arena.IssueD`) of the region of the same base and of size `size + extra` into
364	the place `d` that holds `b` when `grow` starts (DS2-2), on the released state: `reject` when no
365	place holds `b` (there is no destination, §77.2; never on library-reachable states,
366	`DReach.grow_holder`), its static checks (`IssueStatic`, §77.1, §77.2), `fail`, the state
367	unchanged, unless the extension is in place (DS-v1 "fail otherwise", availability §77.4), `split`
368	of `internal` (O2) and `store` of the new block into `d` (O8). -/
369	inductive GrowStep (k : K) (j b extra : Nat) (D : DState) : Outcome3 DState → Prop where
370	  | noStack : D.stacks[j]? = none → GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
371	  | noBlock {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = none →
372	      GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
373	  | release {st : Stack} {x : Blk} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = some x →
374	      ReleaseStep b D.kern .reject → GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
375	  | noHolder {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = some x →
376	      ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) → holderPlace D.kern b = none →
377	      GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
378	  | static {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ : S3} {d : Nat} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
379	      st.block b = some x → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) →
380	      holderPlace D.kern b = some d →
381	      ¬ IssueStatic s₁ st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) d →
382	      GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
383	  | fail {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ : S3} {d : Nat} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
384	      st.block b = some x → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) →
385	      holderPlace D.kern b = some d →
386	      IssueStatic s₁ st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) d →
387	      ¬ InPlace st x extra → GrowStep k j b extra D .fail
388	  | split {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ : S3} {d : Nat} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
389	      st.block b = some x → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) →
390	      holderPlace D.kern b = some d →
391	      IssueStatic s₁ st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) d → InPlace st x extra →
392	      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)] s₁ .reject →
393	      GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
394	  | store {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ s₂ : S3} {d : Nat} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
395	      st.block b = some x → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) →
396	      holderPlace D.kern b = some d →
397	      IssueStatic s₁ st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) d → InPlace st x extra →
398	      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)] s₁ (.ok s₂) →
399	      StoreStep s₁.A.length d s₂ .reject → GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
400	  | ok {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ s₂ s₃ : S3} {d : Nat} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
401	      st.block b = some x → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) →
402	      holderPlace D.kern b = some d →
403	      IssueStatic s₁ st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) d → InPlace st x extra →
404	      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)] s₁ (.ok s₂) →
405	      StoreStep s₁.A.length d s₂ (.ok s₃) →
406	      GrowStep k j b extra D
407	        (.ok ⟨s₃, D.stacks.set j (growMeta st x extra s₁.A.length d), D.fresh⟩)
408	
409	/-! ## Library runs (DS-v2; §36, §56, §57) -/
410	
411	/-- One `ok` step of the stack library (DS-v2, non-normative): a kernel step O1–O16 of
412	non-administrative code, the registry unchanged; `newStack` with the guard of §56 against the other
413	registries `others`; `push`, `mark`, `rewind`, `grow`. -/
414	inductive DStep (k : K) : DState → DState → Prop where
415	  | kernel {D : DState} {s' : S3} : KStep k D.kern s' → DStep k D ⟨s', D.stacks, D.fresh⟩
416	  | newStack {D D' : DState} {others : List (List Nat)} {storage i : Nat} :
417	      NewStackStep others storage i D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'
418	  | push {D D' : DState} {j size dst : Nat} : PushStep k j size dst D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'
419	  | mark {D D' : DState} {j : Nat} : MarkStep j D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'
420	  | rewind {D D' : DState} {j : Nat} {m : Mark} : RewindStep k j m D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'
421	  | grow {D D' : DState} {j b extra : Nat} : GrowStep k j b extra D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'
422	
423	/-- States reachable from the initial state by library steps (DS-v2, non-normative; §47). -/
424	inductive DReach (k : K) (statics : Statics) : DState → Prop where
425	  | init : DReach k statics (DState.init statics)
426	  | step {D D' : DState} : DReach k statics D → DStep k D D' → DReach k statics D'
427	
428	/-- Finite sequences of library steps (DS-v2, non-normative; §58 `ok` transitions). -/
429	inductive DRun (k : K) : DState → DState → Prop where
430	  | refl (D : DState) : DRun k D D
431	  | tail {D D' D'' : DState} : DRun k D D' → DStep k D' D'' → DRun k D D''
432	
433	/-- The kernel part of a library step is reached by kernel steps (§36: the abstraction adds no
434	rights to the kernel; Part XIV: `issue` is `split` then `store`, the reset part of `rewind` is
435	`split` then `release`; DS-v2). -/
436	theorem DStep.reachable {k : K} {statics : Statics} {D D' : DState}
437	    (hr : Reachable k statics D.kern) (h : DStep k D D') : Reachable k statics D'.kern := by
438	  cases h with
439	  | kernel hk => exact .step hr hk
440	  | newStack hs => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs; exact hr
441	  | push hs =>
442	    cases hs with
443	    | ok _ _ _ hsp hst => exact .step (.step hr (.split hsp)) (.store hst)
444	  | mark hs => cases hs with | ok _ _ => exact hr
445	  | rewind hs =>
446	    cases hs with
447	    | ok _ _ _ hsp hrl => exact .step (.step hr (.split hsp)) (.release hrl)
448	  | grow hs =>
449	    cases hs with
450	    | ok _ _ hrl _ _ _ hsp hst =>
451	      exact .step (.step (.step hr (.release hrl)) (.split hsp)) (.store hst)
452	
453	/-- The kernel state of every library-reachable state is kernel-reachable (§36, §57; DS-v2). -/
454	theorem DReach.reachable {k : K} {statics : Statics} {D : DState} (h : DReach k statics D) :
455	    Reachable k statics D.kern := by
456	  induction h with
457	  | init => exact .init
458	  | step _ hs ih => exact hs.reachable ih

462	/-- Reading a list after `set` (support for the §46 metadata updates of DS-v2). -/
463	theorem getElem?_set_cases {α : Type} {l : List α} {j i : Nat} {v x : α}
464	    (h : (l.set j v)[i]? = some x) : (i = j ∧ x = v) ∨ (i ≠ j ∧ l[i]? = some x) := by
465	  rw [List.getElem?_set] at h
466	  by_cases hij : j = i
467	  · subst hij; simp only [↓reduceIte] at h; split at h
468	    · cases h; exact .inl ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
469	    · cases h
470	  · simp only [hij, ↓reduceIte] at h; exact .inr ⟨Ne.symm hij, h⟩
471	
472	/-- Reading a list after appending one element (support for the §46 metadata updates of
473	DS-v2). -/
474	theorem getElem?_append_single {α : Type} {l : List α} {x y : α} {i : Nat}
475	    (h : (l ++ [x])[i]? = some y) : l[i]? = some y ∨ y = x := by
476	  rw [List.getElem?_append] at h
477	  split at h
478	  · exact .inl h
479	  · cases hc : i - l.length with
480	    | zero => rw [hc] at h; simp at h; exact .inr h.symm
481	    | succ n => rw [hc] at h; simp at h
482	
483	/-- `takeWhile (· ≠ m)` stops at the first occurrence of `m` (support for the §46 metadata of
484	DS-v2 `rewind`). -/
485	theorem takeWhile_ne_append {m : Mark} : ∀ {pre : List Mark} (post : List Mark), m ∉ pre →
486	    (pre ++ m :: post).takeWhile (fun x => decide (x ≠ m)) = pre
487	  | [], post, _ => by simp
488	  | a :: pre, post, h => by
489	    have ha : a ≠ m := fun e => h (e ▸ List.mem_cons_self ..)
490	    have ih := takeWhile_ne_append (pre := pre) post (fun h' => h (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ h'))
491	    rw [List.cons_append, List.takeWhile_cons]
492	    simp only [ha, ne_eq, not_false_eq_true, decide_true, ↓reduceIte, ih]
493	
494	/-- A prefix of `take` (support for DS-v2 `grow`, §46 metadata: the old cells are a prefix of the
495	new ones). -/
496	theorem take_prefix_take_add {α : Type} : ∀ (l : List α) (n e : Nat), l.take n <+: l.take (n + e)
497	  | [], n, e => ⟨[], by rw [List.take_nil, List.take_nil]; rfl⟩
498	  | _ :: _, 0, _ => ⟨_, List.nil_append _⟩
499	  | a :: l, n + 1, e => by
500	    obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := take_prefix_take_add l n e
501	    exact ⟨t, by rw [Nat.add_right_comm, List.take_succ_cons, List.take_succ_cons,
502	      List.cons_append, ht]⟩
503	
504	/-- The cells of a block are a prefix of the cells of the block grown from the same base (DS-v2,
505	non-normative, "same base"; §46 issued regions). -/
506	theorem cellsOf_prefix (st : Stack) (b n e : Nat) : cellsOf st b n <+: cellsOf st b (n + e) :=
507	  take_prefix_take_add _ _ _

511	  unfold releaseEff; split <;> simp

514	theorem releaseEff_I (s : S3) (a : Nat) : (releaseEff s a).I = s.I := by

528	/-- `rewind_rejects_live_above` (DS-v2, non-normative: "rewind m … rejects if an active authority
529	derived from internal covers a cell above m"): for a live mark `m` of an existing stack (its stack
530	live, DS2-3), if an active authority derived from `internal` covers a cell above `m` (at a position
531	`≥ m.top`, DS2-4), `rewind m`
532	has the outcome `reject` and no other: either the administrative right of §36 fails, or `split` of
533	`internal` on the cells above `m` is rejected, since `internal` no longer has effective `Modify` on
534	that cell (§43, §61.1). -/
535	theorem rewind_rejects_live_above {k : K} {D : DState} {j : Nat} {st : Stack} {m : Mark}
536	    (hst : D.stacks[j]? = some st) (hm : LiveMark D.kern j st m) {x l : Nat} {y : Authority}
537	    (hy : D.kern.A[x]? = some y) (ya : y.active = true) (hx : st.internal ∈ D.kern.ancs x)
538	    (hly : l ∈ y.footprint) (hl : l ∈ above st m) :
539	    RewindStep k j m D .reject ∧ ∀ o, RewindStep k j m D o → o = .reject := by
540	  have hn : ¬ SplitPre k D.kern st.internal [above st m] := fun h =>
541	    no_desc_of_modify hy ya hly hx (h.modifyOn _ (List.mem_singleton_self _) l hl)
542	  refine ⟨?_, fun o ho => ?_⟩
543	  · by_cases ha : AdminRight D.kern st
544	    · exact .split hst hm ha (.reject hn)
545	    · exact .static hst hm ha
546	  · cases ho with
547	    | noStack h => rw [hst] at h; cases h
548	    | dead h hd => rw [hst] at h; cases h; exact absurd hm hd
549	    | static => rfl
550	    | split => rfl
551	    | release => rfl
552	    | ok h _ _ hsp =>
553	      rw [hst] at h; cases h
554	      exact absurd (Guarded.ok_iff.1 hsp).1 hn

556	/-- `rewind_keeps_older_marks` (DS-v2, non-normative: "otherwise returns those cells to available
557	and removes m and every mark above it"; §46 metadata, §62 `ok` effect): after an `ok` of
558	`rewind m`, the marks of the stack are exactly those older than `m`, its top is the top of `m`
559	(the cells above `m` are available again), the other stacks are unchanged, and no initialization
560	changes. -/
561	theorem rewind_keeps_older_marks {k : K} {D D' : DState} {j : Nat} {m : Mark}
562	    (h : RewindStep k j m D (.ok D')) {st : Stack} (hst : D.stacks[j]? = some st)
563	    {pre post : List Mark} (hs : st.marks = pre ++ m :: post) (hpre : m ∉ pre) :
564	    (∃ st', D'.stacks[j]? = some st' ∧ st'.marks = pre ∧ st'.top = m.top) ∧
565	      (∀ i, i ≠ j → D'.stacks[i]? = D.stacks[i]?) ∧ D'.kern.I = D.kern.I := by
566	  cases h with
567	  | ok hst₀ _ _ hsp hrl =>
568	    rw [hst] at hst₀; cases hst₀
569	    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hsp
570	    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hrl
571	    refine ⟨⟨_, List.getElem?_set_self (lt_of_getElem? hst), ?_, rfl⟩,
572	      fun i hi => List.getElem?_set_ne (Ne.symm hi), ?_⟩
573	    · simp only [rewindMeta]; rw [hs]; exact takeWhile_ne_append post hpre
574	    · rw [releaseEff_I]; rfl

578	/-- Anchors name existing authorities (support for DS-v2, non-normative, `rewind`; §44: `D(q)`
579	holds authority identities; §42: identities index `A`): every anchor of every place is an index of
580	`A`. -/
581	def DBound (s : S3) : Prop := ∀ q, ∀ x ∈ s.D q, x < s.A.length
582	
583	/-- Every kernel step keeps `DBound` (support for DS-v2, non-normative; §60–§75 `ok` effects on
584	`D`, §42): each effect keeps, drops or moves existing anchors, adds an active authority (§64,
585	§65), or replaces an anchor by an element of its origin chain (§73); `A` never shrinks. -/
586	theorem kstep_dBound {k : K} {s s' : S3} (h : KStep k s s') (hb : DBound s) : DBound s' := by
587	  have hA := kstep_akeep h
588	  suffices H : ∀ q, ∀ x ∈ s'.D q, x < s.A.length from fun q x hx => hA.lt (H q x hx)
589	  cases h with
590	  | derive hs => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs; exact hb
591	  | split hs => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs; exact hb
592	  | release hs =>
593	    obtain ⟨hp, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs
594	    obtain ⟨x, hx, -⟩ := hp.active
595	    rw [releaseEff_eq hx]; intro q z hz
596	    simp only at hz; split at hz
597	    · exact hb q z (List.mem_filter.1 hz).1
598	    · exact hb q z hz
599	  | transfer hs =>
600	    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs
601	    intro q z hz; simp only [transferEff] at hz; split at hz
602	    · cases hz
603	    · rcases List.mem_append.1 hz with hz | hz
604	      · exact hb q z hz
605	      · simp only [movedTo, List.mem_flatMap] at hz
606	        obtain ⟨r, -, hr⟩ := hz; exact hb r z hr
607	  | depend hs =>
608	    obtain ⟨hp, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs
609	    intro q z hz; simp only [dependEff] at hz; split at hz
610	    · rcases List.mem_append.1 hz with hz | hz
611	      · exact hb _ z hz
612	      · rw [List.mem_singleton.1 hz]; obtain ⟨y, hy, -⟩ := hp.anchorActive; exact lt_of_getElem? hy
613	    · exact hb q z hz
614	  | enter hs =>
615	    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs
616	    intro q z hz; simp only [enterEff] at hz; split at hz
617	    · cases hz
618	    · exact hb q z hz
619	  | exit hs =>
620	    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs
621	    intro q z hz; simp only [exitEff, List.mem_map] at hz
622	    obtain ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩ := hz
623	    have hxl := hb q x hx
624	    cases hf : firstSurv s s.F.tail (x :: s.ancs x) with
625	    | none => exact hxl
626	    | some w =>
627	      rcases List.mem_cons.1 (List.mem_of_find?_eq_some hf) with rfl | hw
628	      · exact hxl
629	      · exact Nat.lt_trans (chain_lt hw) hxl
630	  | read hs => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs; exact hb
631	  | write hs => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs; exact hb
632	  | writeShared hs => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs; exact hb
633	  | pin hs => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs; exact hb
634	  | unpin hs => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs; exact hb
635	  | endUse hs =>
636	    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs
637	    intro q z hz; simp only [endUseEff, cleanup, endUseS] at hz; split at hz
638	    · cases hz
639	    · exact hb q z hz
640	  | free hs => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs; exact hb
641	  | alloc hs =>
642	    cases hs with
643	    | ok =>
644	      intro q z hz; simp only [allocEff] at hz; split at hz
645	      · cases hz
646	      · exact hb q z hz
647	  | @store a p hs =>
648	    obtain ⟨hp, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs

650	    cases hy : s.A[a]? with
651	    | none => rw [hy] at hd; exact hd.elim
652	    | some y =>
653	      rw [storeEff_eq hy]; intro q z hz; simp only at hz; split at hz
654	      · rcases List.mem_append.1 hz with hz | hz
655	        · exact hb _ z hz
656	        · rw [List.mem_singleton.1 hz]; exact lt_of_getElem? hy
657	      · exact hb q z hz

659	/-- Every kernel-reachable state satisfies `DBound` (support for DS-v2, non-normative; §47: no
660	anchor initially; §57 reachable states). -/
661	theorem dBound_of_reachable {k : K} {statics : Statics} {s : S3} (h : Reachable k statics s) :
662	    DBound s := by
663	  induction h with
664	  | init => intro q x hx; simp [S3.init] at hx
665	  | step _ hs ih => exact kstep_dBound hs ih

667	/-- Shape of the `internal` authority of every stack (DS-v2, non-normative; §76.2: own mode
668	`Modify`; §76.3: its footprint contains the footprint of the storage, the cells of the stack; §42:
669	modes and footprints never change): it exists, has own mode `Modify` and covers every cell. -/
670	def StackShape (D : DState) : Prop :=
671	  ∀ (i : Nat) (st : Stack), D.stacks[i]? = some st →
672	    ∃ y : Authority, D.kern.A[st.internal]? = some y ∧ y.mode = .modify ∧
673	    ∀ c ∈ st.cells, c ∈ y.footprint
674

content.content:
# Readings — datastack (DS-v1, non-normative; spec v0 §36, §38, §46, §47, §56, §58, Part XIV, §82)

Module: `formal/Ern/Lib/DataStack.lean` (namespace `Ern.Lib.DataStack`).
Machine-checked examples: section `Witness` of that module (`run_ok`, `reading_above`,
`reading_order`, `reading_mark`, `reading_grow_dst`, `reading_newStack`, `reading_rewind_right`,
all by `decide` on library-reachable states under `Access.Examples.K0`). Four scratch files outside
the repository, re-elaborated against `b4a5cd3`: `../final5/nostack.lean` (DS-R3),
`../final5/d17.lean` and `../../records-chk/q28split.lean` (DS-R13), `../../records-chk/okonly.lean`
(R3).

Source of the contract: the brief's obligation 6 (DS-v1). Spec v0 does not define it (Part XIV
preamble: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and
are not defined here"). Every entry: clause, reading used, alternative, example whose verdict
changes. "[draft]" = the reading of the draft (`formal/derivability_0.1`, `Lib/DataStack.lean`),
used per policy ("use the draft's reading if the draft matches one of the readings").

## Readings that change verdicts

**DS-R1 "a cell above m" [draft].** DS-v1: "rejects if an active authority derived from internal
covers a cell above m". Reading: the cells at positions `[m.top, top)` (`above`), those that
`rewind m` returns. Alternative A: any cell at position `≥ m.top`. Alternative B: the regions issued
after `m`. Example (`Witness.reading_above`, decided): after `rewind ⟨0,1,1⟩` (top 1) and the
program's `release(5)`, `derive(4, [3], Modify)` gives authority 8, active, derived from `internal`
4, on cell 3 (position 1 ≥ `m0.top` = 0, but ≥ current top). `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is `ok` here; under
A it is rejected. Safety is unaffected: the next `push` over cell 3 is rejected by the effective
right (§43, §61.1). Under B, a block grown after `m` from a base below `m` blocks `rewind` on its
lower part too (draft `opsE4`; not re-run here).

**DS-R2 order of the dead/foreign-mark `fail` and of the right of §36 [draft].** §58: "static
preconditions are checked before dynamic availability, according to the operation's contract";
DS-v1 lists "fails on a dead or foreign mark" first and says nothing about §36. Reading: mark
liveness first (`fail`), then `AdminRight` (`reject`). Alternative: §36 first. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (1)): a callee frame with no right on the stack value rewinds to the
removed mark `⟨0,1,1⟩`: `fail` here, `reject` under the alternative. Consequence: `mark_no_aba`
gives `fail` unconditionally.

**DS-R3 "foreign" mark.** Reading: a mark is live for stack `j` iff `m.stack = j ∧ m ∈ st.marks`
(`LiveMark`); the stack identity is checked explicitly although, under `MarksWF` (proved on every
library-reachable state), membership alone implies it. The explicit identity check changes no verdict
on reachable states.
`rewind` on a stack index that does not exist is `reject` (no stack value) [draft]. This is a reason
to reject that DS-v1 does not list (narrow check ds4-2). Alternative: a mark of a stack that does not
exist is not live, so DS-v1's "fails on a dead or foreign mark" gives `fail`; or DS-v1 is silent.
Example (`../final5/nostack.lean`): on the initial state `d0` (`DReach.init`, no stack),
`rewind(0, ⟨0,0,0⟩)` is `reject` through `RewindStep.noStack` and neither `ok` nor `fail`; `fail` under
the alternative.

**DS-R4 `grow` with `extra = 0` [draft].** DS-v1 says nothing. Reading: `reject` ("grow" means a
larger size). Alternative: an in-place re-issue of the same region. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (2)): `grow(0, 5, 0)` in `d9` is `reject`, while release, static checks,
in-place check, `split` and `store` of the same region are all `ok` (alternative: `ok`).

**DS-R5 `grow` of a live block that cannot extend in place: `fail`** (libs.md C10; DS-v1 "fail
otherwise"). The draft rejected it. Reading: the in-place check (`InPlace`: the block ends at the top
and `extra` cells follow) is the availability check of the derived issue (§77.4) and gives `fail`.
Example (`Witness.run_ok`): `grow(0, 5, 1)` in `d7`, where block 6 lies above block 5, is `fail`.
A `b` that is no block of the stack (`Stack.block` gives none): DS-v1 says nothing. Reading [draft
`case_grow`]: `reject` (`GrowStep.noBlock`). Alternative: `fail`, by analogy with DS-v1 "rewind m
fails on a dead or foreign mark" (an identifier the stack does not record). Example
(`Ern.Corpus.DataStack.DS03`, conjunct `GrowStep K0 0 6 1 ds03 .reject`, decided): after
`grow(0, 6, 1)` replaced block 6 by block 9 (`ds03.stacks` records the blocks `[⟨0, 3, 9, 5⟩]`
only), `grow(0, 6, 1)` is `reject` here and `fail` under the alternative (the step reaches
`noBlock` and no other rule).

**DS-R6 order inside `grow`.** The derived issue's static checks (`IssueStatic`) cannot be read on
the state before the release of `b` (the destination still holds `b`, §77.2 "holding no active
authority"). Reading: block lookup and `0 < extra` (`reject`); `release(b)` (`reject` if refused);
`IssueStatic` on the released state (`reject`); `InPlace` (`fail`, the state unchanged); `split`;
`store`. Alternative: in-place `fail` before the release. Changes the verdict when `b` cannot be
released and the block is not in place (`reject` here, `fail` under the alternative).

**DS-R7 `push` without room: `fail` [draft].** DS-v1 says only that `push` uses the derived issue.
Reading: the `size` cells at the top must exist (`top + size ≤ |cells|`); otherwise `fail`
(availability, §77.4), checked after `IssueStatic` on the requested cells that exist. Alternative:
"region belongs to the administered storage" (§77.2, static) gives `reject`. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (3)): `push(0, 3, 4)` on a stack of 2 cells is `fail`.

**DS-R8 `push` static checks are those of the derived issue (`Arena.IssueStatic`, §77.1, §77.2).**
Not the draft's restricted ones: an `Init` destination is not rejected (spec v0 §77.2, O8.2).
`push` of size 0 is accepted (issue of the empty region): the empty block blocks no `rewind`, and
`rewind` forgets it in the metadata while its authority stays active [draft DS-3].

**DS-R9 `newStack` preconditions: §76.5 applies [draft]** (was R5; review round 2, DS-1). DS-v1
says nothing about creation. Reading: those of `newArena` other than its guard
(`Arena.NewArenaBase`: §76.1–§76.3 and §76.5 "All leaves of the arena value holding `internal` are
already `Init`", read for a stack) and `Guard56 (stackInternals :: others)` (§56). Alternative: drop
§76.5 for a stack (DS-v1 does not take over `newArena`). Same choice as H-R8 for pools. Example
(`Witness.reading_newStack`, decided on the initial state of statics `wsu`): leaf 0, `Uninit`, owns
the storage leaf 1 and so holds its root authority 1 (§47); `newStack(1, 1)` is `reject` (only
§76.5 fails: every other field of `NewArenaBase` and the guard hold), `ok` under the alternative.

**DS-R10 `mark` requires no right [draft]** (was R6; review round 2, DS-1). DS-v1 says nothing about
a right for `mark`. Reading: `ok` on an existing stack, `reject` on a missing one; `mark` changes
library metadata only and creates no right (§36 ¶2, §38). Alternative: §36 ¶1, metadata is modified
"to the extent permitted by the applicable rights and contracts", so `mark` needs a right on the
stack value (`AdminRight`, or a valid `writeShared` over it, §68), else `reject`. Example
(`Witness.reading_mark`): in `d13` (a callee frame entered after the rewind), the callee has no
`AdminRight`, no `Observe` right on the stack value 0 and no valid `writeShared` over it through any
authority; `mark(0)` is `ok` (a mark appended), `reject` under the alternative.

**DS-R11 `grow` destination: the recorded `Blk.dst` [draft]** (was R7; review round 2, DS-1). DS-v1
says only "grow is in place only" and "uses the derived issue"; it does not name the destination.
Reading: the destination recorded for the block at `push` (`Blk.dst`), even when the block value has
been transferred since and that place is `Moved`. Alternative: the place that currently holds `b`.
Changes the arrival state. Example (`Witness.reading_grow_dst`): after the first push (block 5
stored at place 4), the program's `transfer(4, 5)` (§63) moves authority 5 to place 5 and makes
place 4 `Moved` (`d14`). `grow(0, 5, 1)` is `ok` and stores the new block authority 6 into place 4,
which becomes `Init` (§65), while place 5 keeps the released authority 5 (`d15`). Under the
alternative, the static checks of the derived issue (`IssueStatic`) and `store(6, 5)` are `ok` on
the same released and split state, and authority 6 is held by place 5.

**DS-R12 reasons for which `rewind` rejects: §36 applies** (B47). DS-v1: "rewind m fails on a
dead or foreign mark, rejects if an active authority derived from internal covers a cell above m,
otherwise returns those cells to available and removes m and every mark above it". It names one
reason to reject. Reading: §36 applies too (normative: `MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable on
the stack value; the abstraction adds no rights to the kernel), so `rewind` rejects without
`AdminRight`. On library-reachable states and for an existing stack, this is the only reason outside
DS-v1's list (`rewind_ok_iff`, R3; that `ok` is then the only outcome is stated by `RewindStep.det` since `b2dcaa9`; before, it
follows from `Guarded.det`, R3). A stack index with no stack gives `reject` for another reason
outside the list, `RewindStep.noStack` (DS-R3). Alternative: DS-v1's list is exhaustive, so
`rewind` is `ok` whenever the mark is live and no such authority covers a cell above it. Example (`Witness.reading_rewind_right`,
decided): `d16` is reached by the rewind to `⟨0,1,1⟩`, the program's `release(5)` and a callee frame
with no parameter or local. There, mark `⟨0,0,0⟩` is live for stack 0 and no active authority
derived from `internal` 4 covers cell 2, the cell above it. `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is `reject` here and
`ok` under the alternative. The kernel sequence cannot realize the alternative: `split` of
`internal` also rejects in `d16`, because `internal` is not exercisable at `Modify` (§61.1).
`AdminRight` has two conjuncts. `d16` tests only `MetaRight` (`internal` is active there); the other
conjunct, `internal` active, is DS-R13.

**DS-R13 a live mark of a dead stack** (narrow check ds4-3). DS-v1: "the stack keeps the ordered list
of live marks; rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark". It does not speak of a dead stack. §46:
"The arena is **live** if `internal` is active", read for a stack by `AdminRight`. Reading:
`reject` (`RewindStep.static`), forced by the §61.1 check of the derived reset; also by the
`Active internal` conjunct of `AdminRight`. Alternative 1: DS-v1's list is exhaustive (the DS-R12
alternative): `ok`. Alternative 2: a mark of a dead stack is a dead mark: `fail` (under the DS-R2 order the mark is
checked first). Example (`../final5/d17.lean`: `d17_facts`, `d17_only_reject`): `d17` is `d11` (the
rewind to `⟨0,1,1⟩` and the program's `release(5)`) followed by the program's `release(4)` of
`internal` 4. Mark `⟨0,0,0⟩` is live for stack 0, no active authority derived from `internal` covers
cell 2, `MetaRight` still holds and `internal` is inactive. `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is `reject` and nothing
else here, `ok` under alternative 1 and `fail` under alternative 2. The kernel sequence cannot
realize alternative 1: in `d17`, `split` of `internal` rejects because `internal` is inactive (§61.1;
`SplitPre.active`, the same test as the first conjunct of `AdminRight`). Without that conjunct the
outcome stays `reject` through `RewindStep.split` (`../../records-chk/q28split.lean`,
`d17_split_rejects`). So whether the liveness of the stack is part of the §36 check does not change
the verdict. The only alternatives that change it are alternative 2 (`fail`) and alternative 1
(`ok`), and alternative 1 is possible only if `rewind` skips the derived reset.

## Readings that change no accepted program (representation)

- **R1 State.** `DState = ⟨kern, stacks, fresh⟩`, separate from `S3` (§38, §46); a stack is its
  registry index, stacks are never removed; `fresh` is a global counter (§9 "a monotonically
  increasing counter is one possible representation"). The arena registry is not in `DState`: the
  guard reads it through the parameter `others` (§56), as `Arena.NewArenaPre` reads stacks through
  its `others`.
- **R2 Available cells** = positions `≥ top` of the ordered cells (`Stack.entry.available =
  cells.drop top`); `push` and `grow` take cells at the top only and `rewind` returns exactly
  `above`, so this is a set of leaves as in §46.
- **R3 `rewind` kernel part [draft]:** the derived reset of Part XIV restricted to `above st m`:
  `split(internal, [above])` then `release` of the new authority. Plus an explicit §36 check
  (`AdminRight`: `internal` active and `MetaRight` on the stack value) before the split, like
  `IssueStatic.live/metaRight`. **Exact outcome** (`rewind_ok_iff`, hypothesis: the state
  invariant `DReach` only, no `KInv`, no I3): for an existing stack, `rewind m` has an `ok` outcome iff `m` is
  live for the stack (DS-v1), `AdminRight` holds (§36), and no active authority derived from
  `internal` covers a cell of `above st m` (DS-v1). The model does not check the DS-v1 condition
  explicitly. It is the effective `Modify` of `internal` that `split` requires (§61.1, effective
  mode of §43; §61.3 follows). No other check of `split` or `release` rejects on such a state:
  - `internal` has own mode `Modify` and covers the cells (`DReach.stackShape`: §76.2 and §76.3 at
